copy.title: Beyond the projects
copy.intro: These topics are not part of my projects, so the live Studio leaves them out. Each one is a short silent screen capture made in the Math Studio. If you want the code and the PDF notes behind a clip, ask for them and I will send them by email once I approve the request.
copy.gallery: Topics outside my projects, as short silent clips. The code and PDF notes are free and are sent on request.
copy.note: Free of cost — shared on approval

groups.title: Molecular dynamics
groups.what: Lennard-Jones argon as gas, liquid and solid (Maxwell–Boltzmann speeds, g(r), diffusion, melting), kinetic theory of collisions, reactive collisions A + B → C with an activation energy and a steric factor, the Arrhenius plot and…

The example's own animation track is scrubbed and the camera swings gently around the 3D view.
Parameters on screen: density ρσ^d = 0.8; temperature T (ε/k_B) = 1; ramp to T₁ (melting / freezing) = 1; thermostat = Berendsen; time steps = 2000; Δt = 0.004.

The Studio has 7 more examples in this group: Argon gas: speeds follow Maxwell–Boltzmann; Argon solid: a crystal (g(r) with sharp peaks); Energy conservation with velocity Verlet (no thermostat); Thermostats: Berendsen vs Andersen, and others.
No code is shown here. The code and PDF notes are free and are shared by email after I approve a request.

The example's own animation track is scrubbed and the camera swings gently around the 3D view.

The example's own animation track is scrubbed and the camera swings gently around the 3D view.
Parameters on screen: azimuth ° = -54.605.

The Studio has 16 more examples in this group: Scaling diag(2, 1, 0.5): volume × 1; Shear: x ← x + 0.8 z (volume kept); Reflection in the plane z = 0 (det −1, the flag is mirrored); Orthogonal projection onto the xy-plane (rank 2, det 0, P² = P), and others.
No code is shown here. The code and PDF notes are free and are shared by email after I approve a request.

groups.title: Arc length

groups.title: Surface area
groups.what: Frustum bands with n → ∞ and one band unrolled flat, cylinder bands that get the area wrong, the circumference-vs-arc-length ribbon, Archimedes' flat strip, a paint coat and a tape that measure S, Gabriel's horn, and Schwarz's…

The example's own animation track is scrubbed and the camera swings gently around the 3D view.
Parameters on screen: y = f(x) = 2*sqrt(x); x from = 1; x to = 2; layers m = m = n (→ 2πrh ✓).

groups.title: Double integrals
groups.what: The region as a heatmap of f·ΔA with its two marginals A(x) = ∫f dy and B(y) = ∫f dx: Fubini says they enclose the same area.
how: Captured from the Math Studio, Double integral workspace, example: Ex 2.21: 4 − x − y on [0, 2] × [0, 1]  (V = 5).
The example's own animation track is scrubbed from start to end and back.
Parameters on screen: f(x, y) = 4 - x - y; x from = 0; x to = 2; y from y₁(x) = 0; y to y₂(x) = 1; sample point in each cell = midpoint.

The Studio has 5 more examples in this group: Ex 2.23: 16 − x² − 2y² on [0, 2] × [0, 2]  (V = 48); Ex 2.25: 3 − x − y on the triangle 0 ≤ y ≤ x ≤ 1  (V = 1); Ex 2.26: between x + y = 1 and the unit circle  (area π/4 − 1/2); The strip trap: 4xy on [0, 1]² with full-height strips  (true 1, trap → 2), and others.

groups.title: Polar integration
groups.what: Polar cells r*·Δr·Δθ (exact annular sectors), the (r, θ) rectangle curling into the region, a pole you can drag anywhere while the rays find their own limits, the forgotten r as ∬ f/ρ dA, the marginal rose A(θ), a coverage map…
how: Captured from the Math Studio, Polar workspace, example: Ex 2.30: inside r = 1 + cos θ, outside r = 1  (area 2 + π/4).
The example's own animation track is scrubbed from start to end and back.
Parameters on screen: f(x, y) = 1; r from r₁(θ) (use theta) = 1; r to r₂(θ) = 1 + cos(theta); θ from = -pi/2; θ to = pi/2.

The Studio has 12 more examples in this group: Ex 2.31: x² + y² on the quarter disk  (π/8); Ex 2.32: e^(x²+y²) on the upper half disk  (π(e − 1)/2); Ex 2.33: 3x + 4y² on the half annulus 1 ≤ r ≤ 2  (15π/2); Ex 2.34: one leaf of r = |cos 2θ|  (area π/8), and others.

groups.title: Phase planes
groups.what: Solver: Phase plane · DE.
how: Captured from the Math Studio, Solver workspace, example: Damped pendulum  θ'' = −sin θ − 0.3 θ'.
The workspace's own Play button runs the simulation and the clip films it as it runs.
Parameters on screen: x′ = f(x, y) = y; y′ = g(x, y) = -sin(x) - 0.3*y; window x0, x1, y0, y1 = -7, 7, -3.2, 3.2; equation = heat u_t = u_xx; iteration = SOR (optimal ω); time / iteration = 1.
